items.title: 66086_Zilner T. Randolph oral history interview
items.q: I says, I have a young man back here on this trombone

ctx.x: MR. RANDOLPH: Whenever you would announce one playing, diplomatically he would show you he wanted to play something else. So this time, so -- he would do this all the time. So I told the audience, I said, ladies and gentlemen, I says, I have a young man back here on this trombone, I says, and I would like for you to hear him play "Russian Lullaby". He plays it so sweetly. I said, his name is Mr. Lawson, stand up, Mr. Lawson. And he comes up there, he says, Mr. Randolph, for these dear people, looking at these…

to another number, and I told him, please excuse Mr. Lawson, he kind of got a little overcome there. And he gets to thinking about his dear old mother and playing that hymn. See, it boomeranged back and he actually was crying.
